name: progress_progressr
title: Use Progressr with Plyr Map-Reduce Functions

origin.description: Return the init, step, and term callbacks plyr expects for .progress.
origin.details: init creates progressor(x, on_exit = FALSE). step calls it. term calls it with type "finish". plyr itself is not called.
origin.value: A named list with init, step, and term.
origin.example:
value <- with_progress({
  bar <- progress_progressr()
  bar$init(3)
  bar$step()
  bar$step()
  bar$term()
  3
}, handlers = handler_void(enable = TRUE), enable = TRUE, interval = 0, delay_terminal = FALSE, delay_stdout = FALSE, delay_conditions = character())
cat("progress_progressr() reports ", value, " steps.\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Return the init, step, and term callbacks plyr expects for .progress.
translation.details: init creates progressor(x, on_exit=False). step calls it. term calls it with type finish. plyr is not called. on_exit is false so the progressor does not finish when init returns.
translation.value: A dict with init, step, and term.
translation.example:
from progressr.evaluate import with_progress
from progressr.external import progress_progressr
from progressr.reporters import handler_void

def body():
    bar = progress_progressr()
    bar["init"](3)
    bar["step"]()
    bar["step"]()
    bar["term"]()
    return 3

value = with_progress(body, handlers=handler_void(enable=True), enable=True, interval=0, delay_terminal=False, delay_stdout=False, delay_conditions=())
print(f"progress_progressr() reports {value} steps.")
